sentences.text: After completion of investigation, the charge sheet was filed and the charges were also framed.

iv) During the investigation of aforesaid FIR, i.e., FIR No.220/2021, the respondent no.1 is stated to have furnished her caste certificate showing that she belongs to a Scheduled Caste, however, the said caste certificate was found not to be genuine.

v) The respondent no.2, thereafter, made a complaint that respondent no. 1 had furnished a caste certificate that is not genuine, which culminated into registration of FIR No. 1121/2021 under Sections 468/471/120B/34 IPC at Police Station Alipur against the respondent no.1.
vi) Aggrieved by the registration of aforesaid FIR No. 1121/2021, the respondent no.1 filed a complaint under Section 200 Cr.P.C. along with application under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C. against the respondent no.2 to 6 herein alleging that one Sanjay, who has been cited as witness in the charge sheet filed in FIR No. 220/2021 has been threatened by the respondent nos. 2 and 3 and his minor son was also beaten.

It was further alleged in para 6 of the complaint that the respondent no.4, who was I.O in FIR No.220/2021 has handed over the caste certificate of the respondent no.1 to the respondent no.2 which was misused by the respondent no.2 for the purpose of getting FIR No.1121/2021 registered against the respondent no.1.

vii) The aforesaid application under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C. filed by the respondent no.1 was allowed vide impugned order dated 18.10.2023, whereby the afore-noted directions have been given to register an FIR against respondent no. 2 - 6 under the Act.
5. The learned APP for the State invites the attention of the Court to the para 13 of the impugned order to contend that the findings recorded therein shows complete non-application of mind.

To appreciate the contention of the learned APP, apt it would be reproduce para 13 of the impugned order, which reads as under:
"13.

The way the DCP has filed the selective report without verifying the allegations as to threatening the witnesses and beating the minor son of one of the witness, itself State Nct Of Delhi vs H & Ors on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197938403/

sentences.text: The allegation in this complainant was of subsequent offences committed against the applicant as well as the witnesses of the complainant but no effort was done to file report after verifying those allegations.
Therefore, this Court is left with no option but to accept the allegations as true.
Even otherwise once complaint of cognizable offence specially under the SC/ST Act is made, it is the duty of the IO/SHO of the PS concerned to register the FIR.
Any failure in this regard is itself an offence under Section 4 of the Act.

Therefore, as the complaint dated 25.072022 as well as complaint of witnesses dated 29.07.2022 shows that atrocities have been committed on the complainants to dissuade them from prosecuting the FIR no. 220/2021, matter requires investigation."...
6. To buttress his contention, the learned APP invites the attention of the
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 01/03/2024 at 21:14:42 Court to the statement of Sanjay, who has been cited as witness in FIR in 220/2021, to contend that the said statement clearly shows that the witness was not extended any threats, therefore, no offence under Section 195(A) IPC is made out.

7. A perusal of the said statement shows that the said witnesses has clearly stated that he is not receiving any threat in the FIR No.220/2021 which shows that the submission of the learned APP is not without substance.

8. In so far as the findings recorded in the impugned order that the DCP has filed a selective report,
the learned APP invites the attention of the Court to the Status Report dated 26.08.2022 of the DCP wherein it has been categorically observed by the DCP that the allegations made in paras 6, 12 and 13 of the complaint could not be substantiated.

9. He submits that there is yet another report of the DCP which is prior in point of time, wherefrom it is also borne out that no threats were extended to the said witness namely Sanjay Singh or to the complainant.
The report also records that the two incidents of quarrel dated 21.07.2022 and 27.07.2022 between both the parties was because of parking issue that was amicably settled between them.
10. Elaborating further, the learned APP submits that since the allegations made in Paras 6, 12 and 13 could not be substantiated, therefore, the respondent nos. 4 to 6 stood exonerated.
Further, there was no recommendation of an administrative inquiry in terms of the proviso to sub- section (2) of Section 4 of the Act.
11. In view of the above, issue notice to the respondents, by all permissible modes, returnable on 03.05.2024.
